title: Transient Priority Bands and Spillover Billing PRD
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Summary: Introduce transient priority bands (TPBs) and a controlled spillover billing mechanism so customers can burst beyond plan entitlements for short windows without immediate hard throttling. TPBs provide per-route and per-model priority weighting that consumes a soft quota first and only charges spillover when soft quotas are exceeded AND spillover budgets are enabled. This PRD defines requirements, edge cases, and acceptance criteria for implementation, billing events, observability, and migration paths.
background: Problem: Customers run heterogeneous workloads with occasional high-priority spikes (e.g., agent orchestration, synchronous chat during marketing events) that should not be immediately blocked by monthly quotas. Current hard quota behavior leads to customer friction and support tickets. Objectives: 1) allow controlled, short-term bursts for eligible plans; 2) make billing predictable and transparent; 3) preserve SLOs for host and shared pools; 4) provide admin controls for enterprises to opt in/opt out. Existing related work includes per-route dynamic bursts and credit buckets but lacks explicit per-model priority bands and a deterministic spillover billing calc.
goals:
- Deliver TPBs as a tiered soft-quota system with clear billing semantics.
- Ensure platform can enforce latency SLOs while permitting bursts.
- Generate billing events that map spillover usage to invoices with clear descriptors.
- Provide console UX for visibility and controls (enable/disable spillover, per-route weights).
out_of_scope:
- Major changes to core runtime scheduling (we will rely on existing autoscaling and routing fallbacks).
- Complex per-token price negotiation for each model — initial roll-out uses per-model class multipliers (low/medium/high compute).
- Billing refund automation (handled by separate billing ops playbook).
proposed_solution: 1) Priority bands: Define three transient priority bands (Low, Elevated, Critical). Each customer plan maps default per-route weights to a band. 2) Soft quota: For each billing window, allocate a small soft quota that can be consumed by TPB bursts without immediate overage charges. 3) Spillover: When combined consumption (soft + steady) exceeds plan entitlement + soft quota, charge spillover at a transparent per-unit rate. 4) Eligibility & controls: Allow org admins to toggle spillover and set per-route max band allowed. 5) Billing events: Emit 'spillover.usage' events with metadata: org_id, route_id, model_class, band, tokens, unit_price. 6) Observability: Console shows current soft usage, projected spillover if sustained for 1 hour, and last 30-day burst histogram. 7) Safeguards: Auto-fallback to lower model variants when sustained burden threatens SLOs; respect enterprise opt-out.
detailed_spec: Spec highlights: - Schema: Add fields to entitlement model: tpbs_enabled (bool), soft_quota_tokens (int), per_route_weight (float), model_class_multiplier (string: 'low'|'med'|'high'). - Runtime enforcement: request router checks band permission and soft_quota; if exceeded, mark token as spillover and route to billing meter. - Billing calc: spillover_charge = ceil(spillover_tokens / 1000) * (base_price_per_k + model_class_multiplier). For simplicity, base_price_per_k is plan-tier configured. - Events & logs: every spillover event emits to billing topic with trace_id for reconciliation. - Console: toggle controls, per-route slider (0-1) that scales soft_quota draw rate. - Backfill: any changes to multipliers affect future windows only.
acceptance_criteria: TPB feature flag deployable and togglable at org-level with default OFF for free-tier and ON for business/enterprise.
Billing emits 'spillover.usage' events with required metadata (org_id, route_id, model_class, band, tokens, unit_price) and these events reconcile with invoice line-items in billing system.
Console exposes: current soft quota remaining (tokens), projected 1-hour spillover cost, and per-route weight control; UI renders without performance regressions.
Runtime enforces per-request band checks and routes tokens tagged as spillover to billing meter; unit tests and integration tests cover normal, bursty, and sustained scenarios.
Automatic fallback to pre-configured lower-cost model variants when sustained spillover would degrade node-level SLOs; verified in chaos test harness.
At least two pilot customers complete UAT and confirm billing preview matches actual billed spillover within 1% variance for a 7-day pilot.
Migration: existing customers with legacy burst credits are mapped to equivalent soft_quota_tokens and an export of mapping is available for audit.
Monitoring: dashboards show soft quota utilization, spillover tokens per org, top routes by spillover, and alerting thresholds when projected 24h spillover > $X (configurable).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): feature-flagged rollout to internal orgs and staging; validate billing events and console UX. Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 2 enterprise customers (billing credits agreed) for 2 weeks. Phase 3 (gradual): open to business and enterprise customers, opt-in for lower tiers. Phase 4 (GA): Default enabled for eligible tiers with full docs and webhook notifications. Rollback: org-level toggle + global kill-switch; billing system reclassifies unbilled spillover as blocked if rollback occurs mid-window and triggers ops ticket for reconciliation.
migration_plan: - Export existing burst/credit buckets and run mapping script to compute equivalent soft_quota_tokens. - Notify customers 30 days before migration with preview invoice. - Provide opt-out CLI/API to keep legacy behavior for two billing windows. - Data migration runs during low-traffic window; provide reconciliation report after first billing cycle.
open_questions: What default soft_quota size makes sense by plan tier (proposal: Free 0, Pro 5M tokens, Business 50M tokens, Enterprise configurable)?
Should spillover pricing be time-decayed (cheaper for the first 5 minutes of burst) or flat?
How to represent multi-route bursts where multiple small routes collectively exceed soft quota—do we apply pro-rated spillover per route or per-org first?
Edge case: disputed spillover charges—what is final TTL for adjusting billed events (proposal: 45 days with audit trail)?

success_metrics:
- <5% increase in support tickets related to 'quota blocking' in first 30 days post-GA.
- 2 pilot customers complete pilot with invoice variance <1%.
- Less than 0.5% impact on average request latency due to tagging and checks.
- Billing reconciliation success rate > 99.9%.
implementation_notes: Engineering to add feature flag 'tpb.v1'. Start with model_class multipliers configurable by plan. Implement lightweight in-memory counters with periodic flush to billing queue. Use existing chargeback ledger for invoice mapping. Ensure trace_ids propagate from request to billing events.
